newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt welcomes Netanyahu apology on pig posters.
newsitem.headline: Egypt welcomes Netanyahu apology on pig posters.

text.p: Egypt welcomed on Wednesday Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's apology for offensive posters in the West Bank town of Hebron but added that Jewish settlement there created an atmosphere of anti-Moslem extremism.
In his first public comment on the posters, which showed the Prophet Mohammad as a pig, Moussa said: "These statements (by Netanyahu) are excellent and must be taken into consideration."

Israeli police said on Saturday they had arrested a 25-year-old Jewish woman from Jerusalem suspected of pasting the posters on 20 storefronts. Israeli troops have shot and wounded dozens of Arabs protesting at the posters.

Moussa said: "Responsibility lies with the settlers and especially with the woman settler. The atmosphere surrounding settlement is a very extremist atmosphere against the Palestinians and hence against Islam and Moslems.
"The settlers must come to their senses and work for peaceful coexistence with them, each in the context of his own state," the minister added.
